description: Finds every Bible reference in a piece of running text — a sermon, a manuscript, an article — and says for each one where it stands (line and column), whether it exists, and what the verses say, so a quotation can be compared with the text it cites. A reference that points past the end of a chapter or book is reported as a problem. Book names must be capitalised, as in text written for a reader.

edition.description: Edition to quote the verses from: osnb (Norwegian Bokmål), osnn (Norwegian Nynorsk), osen (English), sblgnt (Greek New Testament) or tanach (Hebrew Old Testament). Default: the edition for `language`.

first_line.description: Line number of the first line of `text`, when it is a part of a longer file. Default: 1.

include_text.description: true quotes the verses each reference points at; false gives only where each reference stands and whether it exists. Default: true.

language.description: Language for names, notes and study content, and for the links to bible.flogvit.com: en (English), nb (Norwegian Bokmål), nn (Norwegian Nynorsk), sv (Swedish), fr (French), es (Spanish), fi (Finnish), de (German). Content missing in a language falls back to English. Default: en.

mapping.description: Verse numbering the text cites in, so a reference is checked against that numbering and its verses quoted from it: a mapping id from list_verse_mappings, e.g. "english_kj" or "dnb2024_nb", or a short name such as "kjv". A sermon citing the King James Version has a Malachi 4; osnb does not. Default: osnb.

text.description: The text to check, at most 20000 characters. Split a longer text by lines and pass first_line.

name: check_references

problems.description: How many of them do not exist.

references.description: Every reference found, in the order it stands in the text.

column.description: Column where the reference starts, from 1.

line.description: Line the reference stands on, counted from first_line.

problem.description: Why the reference does not exist, e.g. a verse past the end of the chapter.

reference.description: The passage it points at, written out; absent when it could not be read.

written.description: The reference as it is written in the text.

title: Check the Bible references in a text
